record.context_brief: time-symmetry breaking in extended quantum state spaces
record.original_question: Can time-symmetry breaking and a second-law-like monotone H-function be incorporated into quantum mechanics by extending the quantum state space to a rigged, structured Hilbert space or Gelfand space whose extra structure reflects collective and cooperative macroscopic systems?

evidence.quote: In this direction, some attempts try to incorporate time-symmetry breaking, extending quantum mechanics to a general space state, a 'rigged' (or 'structured') Hilbert space or Gelfand space, with characteristics (superstructure) mirroring the internal structure of collective and cooperative macroscopic systems.

This formulation of dynamics constitutes an effort towards including the second law of thermodynamics, as displayed explicitly by a H-function of the Boltzmann type, which decreases monotonically and takes its minimum value when unstable systems have decayed or when the system reaches equilibrium.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space carrying a unitary one-parameter group $U(t)=e^{-iHt}$ generated by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H$ that models a many-body quantum system whose macroscopic description exhibits collective and cooperative behavior. A rigged Hilbert space (Gelfand triple) is a triple
$$\Phi \subset \mathcal{H} \subset \Phi',$$
where $\Phi$ is a nuclear topological vector space densely and continuously embedded in $\mathcal{H}$ and $\Phi'$ is its topological antidual. The extension of $U(t)$ to $\Phi'$ may, in general, only define a semigroup on suitable subspaces, breaking the time-reversal symmetry present at the level of $\mathcal{H}$.

The problem is to determine whether one can construct a rigged Hilbert space $\Phi \subset \mathcal{H} \subset \Phi'$ together with additional ("superstructure") topological/algebraic data on $\Phi$ that encodes the internal organization of the collective and cooperative degrees of freedom of the underlying macroscopic system, and a functional
$$\mathcal{H}_B : \Phi' \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R},\qquad (\rho,t) \mapsto \mathcal{H}_B(\rho,t),$$
playing the role of a Boltzmann-type $H$-function, such that the following hold simultaneously:

1. The dynamics induced by $H$ on $\Phi'$ restricts to a strongly continuous one-parameter semigroup (rather than a group) on a physically distinguished subspace of $\Phi'$ containing the resonant (decaying) states, thereby realizing an intrinsic arrow of time.

2. For every admissible initial state $\rho_0 \in \Phi'$ evolving under this semigroup to $\rho(t)$, the function $t \mapsto \mathcal{H}_B(\rho(t),t)$ is monotonically nonincreasing for $t \ge 0$ and attains its minimum precisely when all unstable (resonant) components have decayed or the system has reached an equilibrium state.

3. In the limit in which the "superstructure" on $\Phi$ is trivial, the construction reduces to standard unitary quantum mechanics on $\mathcal{H}$.

Decide whether such a rigged Hilbert space, dynamical semigroup, and $H$-functional can be constructed in full generality for quantum systems with collective and cooperative macroscopic behavior, and characterize the class of Hamiltonians $H$ for which this is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: The program of incorporating time-symmetry breaking and a monotone H-function into quantum mechanics via rigged Hilbert spaces (Gelfand triples) has been pursued by the Brussels–Austin School (Prigogine, Bohm, Antoniou, Sudarshan, and others), with partial successes for specific resonance models (Gamow vectors, upside-down harmonic oscillator, Friedrichs model) producing semigroup evolutions and microscopic arrows of time. However, a general framework providing a universal Boltzmann-type monotone H-function on a rigged Hilbert space whose superstructure reflects arbitrary collective/cooperative macroscopic systems remains an open foundational question.

status_evidence.title: Rigged Hilbert Space Resonances and Time Asymmetric Quantum Mechanics
status_evidence.snippet: the symmetry between the resonant and antiresonant states is automatically broken, with resonant states becoming dominant for t > 0 and anti-resonant states becoming dominant for t < 0
status_evidence.claim: Partial results: time-asymmetric semigroup dynamics realized for resonance states in rigged Hilbert spaces.

status_evidence.title: The Rigged Hilbert Space Formulation of Quantum Mechanics and its Implications for Irreversibility
status_evidence.snippet: intrinsic irreversibility is incorporated within the Rigged Hilbert Space quantum mechanics of the Brussels School
status_evidence.claim: Framework exists for incorporating irreversibility via rigged Hilbert spaces, but a universal H-function for general collective systems is not established.

status_evidence.snippet: Time symmetry in Rigged Hilbert Spaces
status_evidence.claim: The status of time-symmetry breaking within rigged Hilbert space quantum mechanics is still under active discussion.
